summary: Updates RFC 4271 to forbid using Autonomous System number 0 in BGP OPEN messages and in AS_PATH, AS4_PATH, AGGREGATOR and AS4_AGGREGATOR attributes of UPDATE messages.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7607 says BGP must not use AS 0 as a peer or in specified route attributes. Routers reject routes containing it so a resource holder can signal that address space should not be routed.

questions: what happens when bgp receives as 0
is as number 0 valid in bgp
why does a roa use as 0
subtitle: BGP rules that reserve AS 0 and reject routes that use it.

tldr.problem: AS 0 is reserved, but earlier BGP specifications did not clearly state how speakers should handle it in messages and route attributes.
tldr.mechanism: A BGP speaker must not originate or propagate AS 0 in specified path and aggregator attributes, and must reject a peer that claims AS 0 in OPEN.
tldr.outcome: The rules codify rejection of AS 0 routes, supporting its use in a Route Origin Authorization to mark address space as not to be routed.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 7607's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC updates RFC 4271 with rules for processing AS 0.

sections.title: Clarifying What AS 0 Means in BGP
sections.content:
AS 0 was listed as reserved and available to identify non-routed networks, but the BGP specifications did not clearly prohibit it in all relevant places. The RFC clarifies how BGP should handle AS 0 in connection setup and route information.

A Route Origin Authorization can list AS 0 as the only origin for a prefix to signal that the prefix and its more-specific prefixes should not be routed. BGP implementations need to reject or not propagate routes containing AS 0 for this signal to work.
sections.plainLanguage: AS 0 can mark an address range as not intended for routing. BGP needs a clear rule to ignore routes that use that reserved number.

sections.title: BGP Behavior for AS 0
sections.content:
A BGP speaker must not originate or propagate a route with AS 0 in AS_PATH, AS4_PATH, AGGREGATOR, or AS4_AGGREGATOR. An UPDATE containing AS 0 in AS_PATH or AGGREGATOR is malformed and follows the error procedures specified in RFC 7606; AS4_PATH and AS4_AGGREGATOR follow RFC 6793 procedures.

If a speaker receives peer AS 0 in an OPEN message, it must abort the connection and send a NOTIFICATION with the OPEN Message Error and Bad Peer AS subcode. A router must not initiate a connection claiming to be AS 0.
sections.plainLanguage: A router must reject AS 0 as the neighbor's identity and must not send routes that contain it in the listed attributes. Different UPDATE attributes use their specified error-handling procedures.

sections.title: Preventing Routes for Reserved Address Space
sections.content:
The RFC explains that a resource holder can publish a Route Origin Authorization with AS 0 as the only valid origin to say that a prefix is not in use for routing. If BGP implementations ignore routes that contain AS 0, a malicious party cannot use such a route announcement to hijack those resources.

The document also makes BGP behavior on receiving AS 0 more precisely defined.
sections.plainLanguage: Ignoring AS 0 routes helps prevent a route announcement from claiming address space that its holder marked as unrouted. The rule also makes router behavior more consistent.
